catalog.title: An exact six-period correction to the printed elliptic billiard assertion k108

metadata.title: An exact six-period correction to the printed elliptic billiard assertion k108
metadata.description:
Two strictly convex primitive six-period billiard trajectories in x²/4+y²=1, sharing a nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, give exact unequal values 11664/3125 and 3645/1024 for the literal k108 quotient in Table 2 of Reznik–Garcia–Koiller (arXiv:2004.12497v11 and the 2021 journal version). The horizontal coordinates and caustic are explicitly credited to Garcia–Reznik, arXiv:2011.06640v1, Appendix B.5.1 (12 November 2020), and its 2022 published successor. Connected family and symmetry machinery are credited to Stachel. This is an attributed corrective application, not new six-period geometry or a claimed all-period repair. Historical firstness and independent discovery are unconfirmed.

catalog.title: A four-period counterexample to the conjectured elliptic billiard invariant k107

metadata.title: A four-period counterexample to the conjectured elliptic billiard invariant k107
metadata.description:
We refute the literal unproved k107 product retained in Table 2 of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller's 2020 preprint and 2021 article. Two primitive convex four-periodic billiard trajectories in the ellipse with semiaxes 4 and 3, sharing the same strictly nested confocal elliptical caustic, give exact values 288/625 and 625/1152 for (A'/A) times the product of original internal half-angle sines. A self-contained continuous-family proof checks physical reflection, strict caustic contact interiors and all denominators.

The general four-periodic construction, its caustic and area identities are credited to Garcia and Reznik. Ferudun's contemporary note (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23075934) contains the same exact correction and is explicitly cited. The original repository disclosure has September 30, 2026 provider dates, before the retrieved October 1 deposit; no exclusive priority or independent discovery is claimed. A bounded primary-source audit and its separately unidentified in-preparation manuscript access limit are disclosed. No corrected all-period invariant is asserted.

catalog.title: An explicit joint Laplace transform for Brownian first-visit cell lengths on a circle

metadata.title: An explicit joint Laplace transform for Brownian first-visit cell lengths on a circle
metadata.description:
We give a complete analytic-transform answer to Georgakopoulos's finite-particle circle first-visit cell-length question in Oberwolfach Report 23/2018, printed p. 1452. For arbitrary fixed distinct labeled seeds, equally spaced seeds, and independent uniform seeds, the full joint Laplace transform is an absolutely convergent series with coefficients reduced to finite permutation sums and deterministic integrals of explicit interval-exit kernels over cumulative physical-clock inequalities. A uniform factorial bound controls the outer series, and compact-support moment determinacy fixes the joint measure. No named density, fast algorithm, or certified inner numerical quadrature is claimed.

Earlier competing-walk painting results and classical heat-kernel, strong-Markov and moment methods are credited. A bounded primary-source audit dated October 7, 2026 did not identify a prior complete characterization of the general target law. catalog.title: The vertex centroid of focal antipedals of even elliptic billiards

metadata.title: The vertex centroid of focal antipedals of even elliptic billiards
metadata.description:
We prove invariant k405 for the original-polygon, full-line antipedals of elliptic billiards with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic and even least period. The unweighted vertex centroid is zero for the center pole and has an explicit phase-independent focal coefficient determined by the axes, caustic parameter, period and perimeter. The proof covers primitive star polygons and either orientation; the circle is treated separately. Repeated odd polygons with even list length and hyperbolic or degenerate caustics are outside the theorem. A self-contained finite-action and perimeter-stationarity proof and portable exact verification supplement are supplied.

This answers k405 as posed without proof in Reznik-Garcia-Koiller's 2020/2021 source. Ferudun's later deposited note, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23092466, states the same theorem and coefficient and uses the same pair-and-moment mechanism; that overlap is explicitly credited. A proof was publicly posted in PR140 on September 30, 2026, before the specific overlapping Zenodo record was created on October 1. The bounded primary-source audit did not establish an earlier complete answer. No absolute priority, exclusive theorem novelty, independent-discovery, copying or collaboration claim is made. The problem is not described as still unsolved at this note's publication.

catalog.title: Ordinary Banach–Mazur rigidity of von Neumann algebras

metadata.title: Ordinary Banach–Mazur rigidity of von Neumann algebras
metadata.description: For every fixed complex von Neumann algebra M, an algebra-dependent positive ordinary complex Banach–Mazur threshold ensures that every von Neumann algebra N within that threshold is Jordan *-isomorphic to M. The same threshold works for the canonical preduals. This consequence uses OpenAI's family-295 ordinary bounded self-coefficient Hochschild vanishing theorem at pinned commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a and Roydor's established geometric machinery. Roydor announced the general conditional implication in 2020, while his published Theorem 1.2 assumes separable predual. The note gives an explicit proof extension using deformation stability on two fixed source algebras and reconstruction of odd finite type-I summands from full abelian projections. The cohomology input, multiplication-stability mechanism, geometric estimates and predual reduction are attributed inherited results; no firstness, independently new cohomology solution, universal numerical threshold or reproduced formal verification is claimed. AI tools were used extensively in research, proof development, drafting and verification. Internal adversarial AI audits are not conventional human peer review, and the preprint has not undergone conventional human refereeing. The PDF is separately downloadable; the source supplement contains the standalone TeX source, precise dependency and priority records, proof audits and finite exact mechanism checks, with unchanged Apache-2.0 upstream material retaining its original license. catalog.title: Rational-point undecidability for smooth projective varieties over the rational numbers

metadata.title: Rational-point undecidability for smooth projective varieties over the rational numbers
metadata.description: Combining OpenAI's negative solution of rational Hilbert's tenth problem, with two explicit proof corrections documented in the verification package, and Poonen's established effective transfer, this note proves undecidability of rational-point existence for arbitrary smooth projective geometrically integral varieties over Q. It specifies homogeneous-equation presentations and valid-input oracle use, and rules out a computable uniform bound on the height of one point in terms of presentation size. Dimension and all size parameters may vary. The arithmetic breakthrough is attributed to OpenAI and the geometric reduction to Poonen; no independent solution of rational Hilbert's tenth problem, new geometric reduction, fixed-dimensional theorem, many-one hardness or first-priority claim is made. catalog.title: Nonnegative binary rational hafnians: an exact reduction and approximation and sampling consequences

metadata.title: Nonnegative binary rational hafnians: an exact reduction and approximation and sampling consequences
metadata.description:
This note records a self-contained exact reduction from every even-order symmetric matrix with binary nonnegative rational off-diagonal entries to a simple unweighted perfect-matching count, with polynomial encoding length, an explicit logarithmic integer-weight gadget, exact rational scaling, and weighted matching fibers. Citing the general-graph FPRAS of OpenAI, it derives a uniform rational hafnian FPRAS with exact zero detection and a rigorously specified bounded-bit total-variation approximate sampler.

Logarithmic integer weight removal, binary rational weighted-to-unweighted equivalence, and counting self-reduction are established machinery and credited to earlier work, including Dell and collaborators, McQuillan, and Jerrum, Valiant, and Vazirani. The approximation breakthrough belongs to OpenAI. This is an attributed consequence and implementation note; no first-publication, new reduction, or independent solution of the base approximation problem is claimed. The supplement contains proofs, transparent code, exact finite enumeration and output-law checks, dependency and priority audits, and clean reproduction instructions. Finite checks do not certify the upstream FPRAS. The real upstream Lean statement was inspected, but no independent kernel rebuild was reproduced.

catalog.title: A sharp dyadic threshold in a characteristic-two random-cone construction

metadata.title: A sharp dyadic threshold in a characteristic-two random-cone construction
metadata.description: OpenAI's October 4 torsion-free group-algebra construction fixes a projective-plane order of 128. This note proves that 32 is the least dyadic order at least 4 at which the unchanged seven-extra squared turn weights admit exponential word-mass decay, using an exact three-class quotient and rational upper and lower certificates. Checking every affected estimate carries the source construction to a 532-edge rose. This is a model-specific threshold, not global generator optimality. Classical HNN embedding gives a two-generator realization; the scalar idempotent and absorbed nonzero cyclic projective right module are inherited consequences already recorded in public triage, and remain valid over every characteristic-two field. catalog.title: Output-sensitive sparse factorization over finite fields from dense factorization

metadata.title: Output-sensitive sparse factorization over finite fields from dense factorization
metadata.description: We give a deterministic reduction for complete sparse univariate polynomial factorization over explicitly represented finite fields. The bit cost is polynomial in term count, binary exponent length, field encoding and the total degree of the distinct densely returned factors, with arbitrary binary multiplicities. A sparse numerator and dense denominator are maintained through characteristic-p descent; denominator degree grows by at most the original radical degree per step. Classical Pade reconstruction, logarithmic derivatives, residue multiplicity methods and Cartier sections are attributed to their original sources. The paper also details inherited dense factorization and prescribed-degree irreducible construction consequences of OpenAI family142 through Berlekamp, Shoup and Rai. The upstream prime-field theorem requires family029 general cyclotomic Hecke zero-freeness. No randomness, GRH or integer-factorization oracle is introduced. Construction degree and optional fixed-root degree are numeric dense parameters; no general binary-degree construction/root bound or practical efficiency is claimed. The sparse theorem is not a sparse-output GCD or arbitrary-circuit theorem. Alec Kriebel is the sole author. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. catalog.title: Metric rigidity at the boundary of cubic compactifications

metadata.title: Metric rigidity at the boundary of cubic compactifications
metadata.description: This note deduces a sharp Cartier-index criterion for irreducible normal projective complex klt Fano varieties of positive dimension carrying a weak Kahler–Einstein metric with bounded potentials: an ample Cartier root -K_X = rL with r > dim(X)/2 + 1 forces stable tangent sheaves on finite quasi-etale covers and rigidity of parallel orthogonal complex structures up to sign. The criterion combines the decomposition theorem of Druel–Guenancia–Paun, a Hilbert-polynomial index bound, and local positive-Ricci curvature; products of equal-dimensional projective spaces show that the strict threshold is sharp. For cubic n-folds with n at least 5, the note applies the criterion to identify all fibers of the forgetful map from complex-preserving GH moduli to ordinary metric GH moduli as conjugation orbits, including singular boundary points. This cubic application uses as an external input OpenAI's ordinary-double-point upper gap theorem at repository commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a; that theorem is not reproved here. The complex-preserving cubic GH/GIT comparison is an attributed deduction through Li–Liu's global Reeb minimum and Spotti–Sun's established transfer. Kong–Shen–Zhao–Zhao already publicly state a stronger complex algebraic comparison. Smooth tangent stability, smooth metric rigidity, and the conjugation convention are credited to Peternell–Wisniewski, Spotti, and Odaka–Spotti–Sun. No first-solution claim, scheme or stack comparison, or formal verification is made. The downloadable files are the paper PDF and an archive of original source, verification scripts, scoped audits, and provenance records; third-party manuscripts and reading caches are excluded. catalog.title: The Sperner property of standard graded Artinian complete intersections in characteristic zero

metadata.title: The Sperner property of standard graded Artinian complete intersections in characteristic zero
metadata.description: For every standard graded Artinian complete intersection over an arbitrary characteristic-zero field, the maximum minimal number of generators over all ideals, including nonhomogeneous ideals, equals the largest coefficient of the complete-intersection Hilbert series. This concise note records an immediate consequence of OpenAI's Artinian EGH theorem and the previously published EGH-to-Sperner implication of Harima, Wachi and Watanabe. It makes degree-one elimination, the empty/all-linear case, the all-ideal filtration argument and field scope explicit, with exact integer examples and scoped dependency/priority audits. catalog.title: Bilinear ergodic Hilbert variation for commuting transformations as a consequence of annular triangular variation

metadata.title: Bilinear ergodic Hilbert variation for commuting transformations as a consequence of annular triangular variation
metadata.description: We give an explicit restriction and transference consequence of OpenAI's full annular variation theorem for the triangular Hilbert transform, manuscript dated October 5, 2026, at source commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a. For arbitrary commuting invertible probability-preserving transformations S,T and complex f,g in L3, the symmetric sums H_N=sum_(0<|n|<=N) f(S^n x)g(T^n x)/n, with H_0=0, satisfy a pointwise r-variation estimate in L^(3/2) for every r>2. They have a bounded maximum and converge almost everywhere and in L^(3/2), with maximal-tail convergence in that norm. The proof uses fixed positive-area cell boxes, half-integer radial endpoints, an explicitly summable O(k^-2) signed kernel error, and finite-menu finite-window Calderon transference. The continuous analytic breakthrough is inherited and credited; this note supplies its discrete restriction and ergodic consequence. Classical transference and its modern predecessors are credited, and no first-priority or independent triangular-Hilbert breakthrough claim is made. Scope remains L3 inputs, symmetric odd truncations, commuting transformations and r>2; there is no r=2, noncommuting or one-sided Cesaro claim. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. Automated adversarial audits are not human peer review or formal certification. The relevant Lean artifacts concern an older maximal theorem and do not formally verify full annular variation or this note. catalog.title: Exact semidefinite complexity of the symmetric traveling-salesman polytope

metadata.title: Exact semidefinite complexity of the symmetric traveling-salesman polytope
metadata.description: The exponential real PSD-rank theorem for shifted perfect-matching matrices in the OpenAI Math Release implies that the symmetric traveling-salesman polytope on N cities has exact real semidefinite extension complexity 2^Theta(N), measured by the order of one real PSD matrix (or total block order). This concise consequence note gives explicit data for Yannakakis's established 3n-city face projection, a 2n-city contraction variant, all-city-count padding, an exact affine-slack calculation, and the subset-state flow upper bound 2(N-1)+(N-1)(N-2)2^(N-3). The lower-bound breakthrough is attributed to OpenAI; no new lower-bound method or firstness claim is made. catalog.title: Reduced C*-algebras of the Thompson family: an attributed consequence of nonamenability

metadata.title: Reduced C*-algebras of the Thompson family: an attributed consequence of nonamenability
metadata.description: An attributed consequence note applying OpenAI's nonamenability theorem for standard Thompson F to the published equivalences of Le Boudec and Matte Bon. The reduced group C*-algebras of F, T, the full automorphism group Aut(F), and the abstract commensurator Comm(F) are simple and have their canonical traces as their unique tracial states, by the discrete-group trace theorem of Breuillard, Kalantar, Kennedy and Ozawa. The countable standard circle-overgroup consequence is also recorded. All these simplicity reductions are inherited; T's unique trace was already unconditional. No new simplicity criterion, independent proof of nonamenability, or first-priority claim is made. The conclusions depending on the new input have exactly the same dependency on its validity.
